- [Skip to main content](https://parks.canada.ca/pn-np/bc/gwaiihaanas#wb-cont) - [Skip to "About government"](https://parks.canada.ca/pn-np/bc/gwaiihaanas#wb-info) - [Switch to basic HTML version](https://parks.canada.ca/pn-np/bc/gwaiihaanas?wbdisable=true) ![](https://pcweb2.azureedge.net/-/media/pn-np/bc/gwaiihaanas/WET4/home/gwaiihaanas-homebanner.jpg?modified=20221115180454) # Gwaii Haanas National Park Reserve, National Marine Conservation Area Reserve, and Haida Heritage Site Massive moss-draped cedar and Sitka spruce tower above the Haida people’s ancient carved poles and fallen longhouses on the lush rainforest islands of Gwaii Haanas. Skies fill with bald eagles, bears scavenge salmon on wild beaches and the ocean teems with breaching whales, porpoises and sea lions. Experience a rich, remote landscape and seascape steeped in spirituality, protected by Parks Canada, Fisheries and Oceans Canada and the Haida who draw cultural inspiration from the land and waters of their ancestors. [![](https://pcweb2.azureedge.net/-/media/pn-np/bc/gwaiihaanas/WET4/modules/feature-village.jpg?modified=20221116194315)](https://parks.canada.ca/pn-np/bc/gwaiihaanas/culture/cultural-sites-culturels) ### [Explore ancient Haida village sites](https://parks.canada.ca/pn-np/bc/gwaiihaanas/culture/cultural-sites-culturels) Weathered, carved poles, longhouse ruins and traditional Haida culture are brought to life at five island village archeological sites by knowledgeable resident Haida Gwaii Watchmen. [![](https://pcweb2.azureedge.net/-/media/pn-np/bc/gwaiihaanas/WET4/modules/feature-wildlife.jpg?modified=20221116194315)](https://parks.canada.ca/pn-np/bc/gwaiihaanas/activ/naviguez-cruise) ### [Cruise through an ocean teeming with wildlife](https://parks.canada.ca/pn-np/bc/gwaiihaanas/activ/naviguez-cruise) Sailing or powerboating in waters rich with wildlife offers the most freedom for exploring Gwaii Haanas’ maze of islands. [![](https://pcweb2.azureedge.net/-/media/pn-np/bc/gwaiihaanas/WET4/modules/feature-kayak.jpg?modified=20221116194315)](https://parks.canada.ca/pn-np/bc/gwaiihaanas/activ/experiences-kayak) ### [Kayak up-close to nature](https://parks.canada.ca/pn-np/bc/gwaiihaanas/activ/experiences-kayak) Kayaking encourages slower paced and more intimate experiences with the ocean and its creatures as well as the primordial wilderness and culture of Gwaii Haanas’ network of islands. ## Most requested - [Tour operators](https://parks.canada.ca/pn-np/bc/gwaiihaanas/visit/voyagistes-operators) - [G̱andll K’in Gwaay.yaay](https://parks.canada.ca/pn-np/bc/gwaiihaanas/culture/cultural-sites-culturels/cultural-sites-culturels-4) - [Travelling to Haida Gwaii](https://parks.canada.ca/pn-np/bc/gwaiihaanas/visit/directions) - [Reservations & fees](https://parks.canada.ca/pn-np/bc/gwaiihaanas/visit/tarifs-fees) - [Land-Sea-People Management Plan](https://parks.canada.ca/pn-np/bc/gwaiihaanas/info/plan/gestion-management-2018) - [Haida Gwaii Watchmen](https://parks.canada.ca/pn-np/bc/gwaiihaanas/culture/gardiens-watchmen) - [SG̱ang Gwaay](https://parks.canada.ca/pn-np/bc/gwaiihaanas/culture/cultural-sites-culturels/cultural-sites-culturels-5) - [Camping and accommodation](https://parks.canada.ca/pn-np/bc/gwaiihaanas/activ/camping) ## Visiting Gwaii Haanas ### [Plan your visit](https://parks.canada.ca/pn-np/bc/gwaiihaanas/visit) How to get here, facilities and services, weather, and maps, tide tables and charts. ### [Reservations and fees](https://parks.canada.ca/pn-np/bc/gwaiihaanas/visit/tarifs-fees) Daily visitor fees, camping and program fees, and more. Free admission for youth. ### [Tour operators](https://parks.canada.ca/pn-np/bc/gwaiihaanas/visit/voyagistes-operators) Guided day trips, guided kayak excursions, guided sailboat and powerboat multiday excursions. ### [Activities and experiences](https://parks.canada.ca/pn-np/bc/gwaiihaanas/activ) Things to do, kayaking, bird watching, and at-home activities. ### [Travelling to Haida Gwaii](https://parks.canada.ca/pn-np/bc/gwaiihaanas/visit/directions) Community services, tourism information. ### [Getting to Gwaii Haanas](https://parks.canada.ca/pn-np/bc/gwaiihaanas/visit/planifiez-plan) Self guided trip, or travelling with a licensed tour operator ### [Safety and guidelines](https://parks.canada.ca/pn-np/bc/gwaiihaanas/securite-safety) Wildlife, weather, environment, seasonal safety, and site regulations. ### [Important bulletins](https://parks.canada.ca/pn-np/bc/gwaiihaanas/bulletins) Requirements, restrictions, and closures. ## About Gwaii Haanas ### [Nature and science](https://parks.canada.ca/pn-np/bc/gwaiihaanas/nature) Conservation and science, indigenous knowledge, animals, plants, the environment and ecosystem restoration. ### [Culture and history](https://parks.canada.ca/pn-np/bc/gwaiihaanas/culture) Haida cultural sites, Haida Gwaii Watchmen, Legacy Pole. ### [Stewardship and management](https://parks.canada.ca/pn-np/bc/gwaiihaanas/info) Cooperative management, Land-Sea-People Management Plan, guiding principles, establishment, partners, permits. | | [How to get here](https://parks.canada.ca/pn-np/bc/gwaiihaanas/visit/planifiez-plan) An intimate experience with land and sea awaits those with a sense of adventure and the skills necessary for a wilderness trip. There are no roads into Gwaii Haanas - access is limited to boats and seaplanes. Visitors who come to explore Gwaii Haanas do so either as part of a guided trip, travelling with one of our licensed tour operators, or on a self-guided adventure. ### Contact us Telephone: 250-559-8818 Toll-free: 1-877-559-8818 Email: [gwaiihaanas@pc.gc.ca](mailto:gwaiihaanas@pc.gc.ca) ### Hours of operation Gwaii Haanas is open to visitors. Our peak visitor season is from June through September. ### \#GwaiiHaanas - [Facebook](https://www.facebook.com/GwaiiHaanas/) - [Twitter](https://x.com/ParksCanada) - [YouTube](https://www.youtube.com/playlist?list=PLOe6XX2wBaiaEmsykZc3vR32dkr9ofvwA) - [Instagram](http://www.instagram.com/parks.canada) ## More places to discover with Parks Canada [![](https://pcweb2.azureedge.net/-/media/WET4/proximite-nearby/default/pc-castor-default-beaver-640x360.png?modified=20221126221528)](https://parks.canada.ca/lhn-nhs/bc/gitwangak) ### [Gitwangak Battle Hill National Historic Site](https://parks.canada.ca/lhn-nhs/bc/gitwangak) Climb the mound at Gitwangak Battle Hill and survey the site of a legendary Gitxsan village fort. See the oldest collection of totem poles in British Columbia retained in their original context at nearby Gitwangak Village. [![](https://pcweb2.azureedge.net/-/media/WET4/proximite-nearby/bc/PacificRimNPR.jpg?modified=20221126220951)](https://parks.canada.ca/pn-np/bc/pacificrim) ### [Pacific Rim National Park Reserve](https://parks.canada.ca/pn-np/bc/pacificrim) Catch a wave, or spread a blanket and watch the sun dip below the horizon. From rainforests on land to marine kelp forests at sea, Pacific Rim National Park Reserve embodies the rich natural and cultural heritage of Canada’s west coast. [![](https://pcweb2.azureedge.net/-/media/WET4/proximite-nearby/bc/FSJNHS_most-places_640x360.jpg?modified=20221126220951)](https://parks.canada.ca/lhn-nhs/bc/stjames) ### [Fort St. James National Historic Site](https://parks.canada.ca/lhn-nhs/bc/stjames) Take a self-guided audio tour, meet costumed interpreters, witness a world-famous chicken race and delight your taste buds at the Home Stretch Diner. Our culture is born of respect; and intimacy with the land and sea and the air around us. Like the forests, the roots of our people are intertwined such that the greatest troubles cannot overcome us. We owe our existence to Haida Gwaii. The living generation accepts the responsibility to ensure that our heritage is passed on to following generations. On these islands our ancestors lived and died and here too, we will make our homes until called away to join them in the great beyond._ ## Public Notices Stay up to date on news from the Haida Nation! # Reservations & fees

## Gwaii Haanas National Park Reserve, National Marine Conservation Area Reserve, and Haida Heritage Site

##### The following definitions apply to entry and service fee categories unless otherwise specified

**Adult** \- Person 18 to 64 years of age

**Senior** \- Person 65 years of age or over

**Youth** \- Person 6 to 17 years of age

**[Free admission for youth 17 and under](https://parks.canada.ca/pn-np/bc/gwaiihaanas/visit/tarifs-fees#youth)**

### Reservations

**Reservations for the 2027 season open on February 15, 2027 9:00am PST.**

As you research and plan your Gwaii Haanas trip, ensue you read our [trip planning](https://parks.canada.ca/pn-np/bc/gwaiihaanas/visit) documents, review the relevant [maps and charts](https://parks.canada.ca/pn-np/bc/gwaiihaanas/visit/cartes-maps), and know your trip dates and general route before making your reservation.

When booking, you will need to provide:

- Your trip dates
- Name, age category, email, and postal codes for each person in your group

**Ready to Make Your Reservation?**

Complete the reservation form to initiate your reservation. \*The form will be active as of February 15, 2027. A staff member will contact you to complete the process, and collect payment. Please note that completing the registration form does not guarantee the dates you have selected. You may also call us at 1-877-559-8818 to make your reservation.

\*Please note if visiting between October 1, 2026 – February 15, 2027, call the number above to reserve.

**A reservation must be made a minimum of 5 business days in advance of a planned trip. Please note the Gwaii Haanas office is not open on statutory holidays and weekends.** All visitors must complete a mandatory self-guided online orientation prior to their trip. The link for the orientation will be sent to you once your reservation is complete and payment processed. Your booking receipt and proof of orientation completion must be carried with you while in Gwaii Haanas.

**A note about weather:** Travel in Gwaii Haanas is always weather dependent. Please factor in additional weather days when booking. Entry and exit dates are required to make  your reservation.

Additional questions? Call our office at 1-877-559-8818 and we will be pleased to help you.

**Are you travelling with a tour operator?**

If you are travelling with a tour operator, you will make your reservation, pay your fee, and receive your orientation directly through your operator.

### Free admission for youth 17 and under

As of January 1, 2018, admission to Parks Canada places for youth 17 and under is free! There’s no better time to create lasting memories with the whole family.

Details


#### What is free?

Admission to all national parks, national historic sites, and national marine conservation areas operated by Parks Canada will be provided free of charge.

Free admission for youth only applies to places managed by Parks Canada. It does not apply to provincial parks, territorial parks, municipal and private parks, nor to the many historic sites not managed by Parks Canada.

Please refer to the [full list of Parks Canada places](https://parks.canada.ca/voyage-travel/recherche-tous-parks-all) before you plan your visit to take advantage of free admission for youth.

#### What is not free?

Parks Canada is pleased to offer free admission for youth at our parks and sites, however regular fees still apply for other experiences and services, such as:

- Camping, backcountry and other accommodations
- Radium, Miette, and Banff Upper Hot Springs
- Northern Park Backcountry Camping and Excursion Permit
- Lockage
- Mooring
- Reservation fees
- Guided tours and hikes and programs not usually included with admission
- Some special event fees
- Firewood
- Backcountry overnight use

**Note**: This is not an exhaustive list. Please verify with the location you will be visiting for more information.

# Camping

## Gwaii Haanas National Park Reserve, National Marine Conservation Area Reserve, and Haida Heritage Site

### [Bear aware food caching](https://parks.canada.ca/pn-np/bc/gwaiihaanas/activ/camping/ours-bear)

There is nothing like arriving at a place and feeling pure serenity. That’s what camping in Gwaii Haanas is like.

Pull up to a slice of beach and it becomes yours for the night. Gwaii Haanas has no formal campsites, but many small pebble beaches, sandy stretches, and headlands.

Please leave each place as you found it so that all visitors can share the wilderness experience. As well, try to stay out of sight and sound of other groups.

#### Closures

Some areas are permanently or temporarily closed to [camping/access](https://www.pc.gc.ca/en/pn-np/bc/gwaiihaanas/info/consultations/gestion-management-2018#section7-0).

#### Follow these steps to minimize your "footprint"

##### Keep group size low

- Maximum group size is 12 people on shore at any one time and within sight and sound of other groups. This helps to reduce impact and maintain a wilderness feeling.

##### Location

- Whenever possible, camp on the sand or rock above the high tide line to minimize impact to local vegetation. Choose a spot for gathering and cooking that is least likely to damage shoreline vegetation.

- Camp away from the mouths of streams, especially during salmon spawning season (mid-August on).

##### Campfires/cooking/dishes

![](https://pcweb2.azureedge.net/-/media/amnc-nmca/bc/gwaii/activ/activ1/beach-kitchen-590.jpg?w=590&h=385&as=1&hash=E80064B53F01F7A3092AADCFD791AC0D)

A beach kitchen© Parks Canada / Barb Johnston

- Use a portable stove to cook your food.

- Keep any campfires below the high tide line and away from drift logs. Use driftwood for your firewood not understory branches. Keep the fire small so it burns to ash and the next incoming tide will wash it away.

- Remove charcoal and scatter any rocks used for a hearth. Do not stir the ashes into the sand and gravel, as they will then take longer to wash away.

- Wash your dishes in the ocean with biodegradable soap and sand as a natural scrubber.

- After eating, immediately burn food scraps or bag them securely for packing out. Return fish entrails to the sea. Bears and other animals are quickly attracted to kitchen waste, even if it has been buried. Improperly handled food waste can create a dangerous situation for the next camper.

##### Hang Food

- Bring ropes and a food storage system to [hang food](https://parks.canada.ca/pn-np/bc/gwaiihaanas/activ/camping/ours-bear) out of reach of animals.

##### Reduce garbage

- Reduce the amount of garbage you create. Plan meals so that you don’t have a lot of uneaten food.

- Choose packaging that is lightweight, compact, and reusable.

- Pack out all garbage. Burn toilet paper and paper in your campfire, but do not burn cans, foil, or plastics, or throw these and other garbage into the ocean.

##### Toilet

- Use the intertidal flush. Make your deposit as close as possible to the water line, and cover with a rock afterwards so others do not step on it. Micro-organisms in the marine soil effectively decompose faeces.

- If you have no alternative, you can use the bush. Dig a small 20-centimetre (8-inch) deep hole away from animal trails and at least 100 metres/yards from water sources. Bury waste completely with soil. Never bury toilet paper or feminine hygiene products. Treat feminine hygiene products as garbage and pack out.

- Use small amounts of biodegradable soap when bathing. Select a location near the mouth of the stream and downstream from any place where people gather water for drinking.

![](https://pcweb2.azureedge.net/-/media/amnc-nmca/bc/gwaii/activ/activ1/bear-275.jpg?w=275&h=207&as=1&hash=D2F613C9E631DF95193730CA4328D50D)A bear in the intertidal zone

© Parks Canada / C. Bergman

##### Respect

- Most areas that visitors find suitable for camping have historically been used by the Haida. These locations have important ecological, spiritual, and archaeological values.

- Treat each campsite as an archaeological site. Do not dig through middens or otherwise disturb any historical features.

- Be [Bear Aware](https://parks.canada.ca/pn-np/bc/gwaiihaanas/securite-safety/ours-bears-1)

##### Before you leave your campsite:

- Dismantle beach furniture. Put logs and rocks back in random positions.

- Pick up all garbage including the tiny pieces like twist ties, paper fragments, and tent pegs.

##### Warning

If Gwaii Haanas staff finds an unattended campsite where food, toiletries, garbage, or other wildlife attractants are left out, they will secure the attractants in a tree near the camp. They will leave a note and will follow up with a visit later in the day to ensure that the visitors understand the importance of keeping these materials out of reach of wildlife.

# Visitor safety

## Gwaii Haanas National Park Reserve, National Marine Conservation Area Reserve, and Haida Heritage Site

Gwaii Haanas is a remote location. It is critical that visitors who plan to travel on their own in Gwaii Haanas have the skills and are adequately prepared to be self-sufficient in emergency situations, including equipment failure.

Emergency responses are weather dependent, and thus in foul weather it may be many hours before emergency response personnel reach visitors in distress.Below is a list of the main topics that visitors are expected to understand and prepare for before coming to Gwaii Haanas.

### [Marine navigation and skills](https://parks.canada.ca/pn-np/bc/gwaiihaanas/securite-safety/competences-skills)

Marine navigation and skills are essential to staying safe in remote waters of Gwaii Haanas.

### [Emergency assistance](https://parks.canada.ca/pn-np/bc/gwaiihaanas/securite-safety/urgence-emergency)

There are no cellphone or internet services in Gwaii Haanas. All boats travelling in the area should be equipped with a VHF radio.

### [Weather and marine hazards](https://parks.canada.ca/pn-np/bc/gwaiihaanas/securite-safety/dangers-mer-marine-hazards)

Even on beautiful days the weather can change quickly in Gwaii Haanas. Be aware of both the marine weather forecast and your own observations of the...

### [Bear aware](https://parks.canada.ca/pn-np/bc/gwaiihaanas/securite-safety/ours-bears-1)

The bears found on Haida Gwaii are often seen foraging in the intertidal zone. Do not approach or feed the bears.

### [Kayaking safety](https://parks.canada.ca/pn-np/bc/gwaiihaanas/activ/kayak/equipement-gear)

Use these checklists as a guide. Items and quantities taken will depend on your sail plan, experience and the length and type of trip.

### [Code of ethics for travellers](https://parks.canada.ca/pn-np/bc/gwaiihaanas/visit/voyagistes-operators/ethique-ethics)

We encourage you to be an ecotourist while travelling in Gwaii Haanas or anywhere on Haida Gwaii.

Facilities in and around Gwaii Haanas are minimal. Access is limited to boats and seaplanes. There are no roads, stores, or fuelling facilities. There are a few mooring buoys, two water hoses, and limited navigational aids.

Make daily travel plans flexible to accommodate weather delays. Bring enough fuel and food to last for a few extra days. Carry clothing and equipment for a variety of weather conditions.

This area has significant tidal variation, strong currents, rapidly changing weather, and strong winds that develop with little or no warning. Take the time to learn about the waters you plan to navigate.

If you find yourself in an emergency situation there are several ways you can request help. We recommended calling for help in the following order:

(Depending on how VHF radio repeaters are functioning and satellite service you may have to try one or several options before reaching someone).

**Canadian Coast Guard**

Marine VHF Channel 16. Stay on the channel for an answer. If you don’t get a response in 15 to 20 seconds try again.

By satellite phone (24-hour service): 1-250-363-6611.

**Parks Canada**

By satellite phone (24-hour service): 1-780-852-3100.

Note that Parks Canada staff monitor VHF Channel 16. They are contacted by the Coast Guard to assist with emergency situations, if in the vicinity.

**Haida Gwaii Watchmen**

Marine VHF Channel 6, within line-of-sight of Watchmen villages.

#### Satellite Locator Beacons

In an emergency situation you can use an EPIRB device or PLB.

_Note:_ Radio reception can be unreliable and there is no cell phone coverage in Gwaii Haanas. If your radio is not receiving a signal, try moving to a different, preferably higher, location. If you do not have a radio, use international distress signals like flares, fire and smoke signals, to draw attention to yourself. These should only be used if you have visual contact with another vessel/aircraft; to draw their attention to an emergency situation.
